items.title: One UI 9.5 could let you shoot 360-degree panoramas with your front and rear cameras

 It will use the front and rear cameras to capture up to 360 degrees of your surroundings.

The One UI 9.5 beta is finally here, and we’ve been taking a close look under the hood to spot upcoming features that aren’t yet enabled. We’ve already found evidence of a native Open Gate recording function , and it seems Samsung is prepping yet another new feature for the Camera app.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We found strings in the One UI 9.5 Camera app code that hint at a new feature called “Dual cam panorama.” The existing Panorama mode captures a wide scene by letting users move their phone in one direction. Dual cam panorama could let users capture a complete 360-degree view of their surroundings by using both the rear and front cameras in tandem.

items.title: One UI 9.5 could bring native full-sensor video recording to Galaxy phones
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung is working on a native Open Gate recording option for the Camera app in One UI 9.5. 
 It will let users record video using the entire imaging area of the sensor for more cropping and stabilization options in post-production. 
 The feature will support several frame rates from 24fps to 60fps. 

Samsung has started rolling out the One UI 9.5 beta for the Galaxy S26 series , and it comes with several new features. However, Samsung is also working on plenty of features that aren’t yet enabled in the beta. This includes a new Camera app feature video enthusiasts will love: native Open Gate recording.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

While digging into the new Camera app in One UI 9.5 , we found several strings suggesting that the company is preparing a new option for Open Gate video recording. Open Gate uses the entire imaging area of a camera sensor instead of cropping the footage to a standard widescreen format like 16:9. Since most camera sensors have a 4:3 aspect ratio, Open Gate captures a taller frame, giving users more options for cropping and stabilization in post-production.
items.t: One UI 9.5 could bring native full-sensor video recording to Galaxy phones

items.title: One UI 9.5 could give lost phones a better chance of finding their way home with lock screen IMEI
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung is working on a feature that would let Galaxy users display their phone’s IMEI number from the lock screen. 
 The feature, spotted in One UI 9.5, could help authorities identify and return lost or stolen Galaxy phones to their rightful owners. 
 Google already offers similar functionality, but it’s unclear whether Samsung’s implementation will make it into One UI 9.5’s public release. 

Samsung is directly borrowing a feature from Google that would allow you to always display your phone’s IMEI number on its lock screen. The functionality, which rolled out to Google’s devices in September this year, is a theft protection feature. It leverages the company’s Personal Safety app. Samsung, for reference, doesn’t ship the app on its Galaxy devices, even though it offers Google’s theft protection.

That could soon change as the South Korean tech giant appears to be working on its own implementation that would allow Galaxy users to make their device’s IMEI accessible from the lock screen.
items.t: One UI 9.5 could give lost phones a better chance of finding their way home with lock screen IMEI

items.title: Samsung is building a secure way for Galaxy users to erase their phones in One UI 9.5
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung appears to be working on a new “Secure erase” option for phones running One UI 9.5. 
 The system would overwrite phone today to impeded recovery efforts. 
 Samsung warns that the process is slow, and can’t be interrupted once it begins. 

Considering how much valuable personal data exists on our phones, it’s no wonder that users are interested in keeping that info private, and now Samsung looks like it’s bringing Galaxy owners a new tool to help keep their data safe when getting rid of an old phone.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Modern phones usually encrypt their data by default, and on Android 10 and later, that’s taken the form of file-based encryption . Not only does that help keep your data secure day-to-day, but it also makes it easier to securely erase the device when you’re getting rid of it, as everything important is already scrambled, highly limiting its usefulness even if a dedicated adversary were to attempt retrieving it.
items.t: Samsung is building a secure way for Galaxy users to erase their phones in One UI 9.5

items.title: Google’s mandatory foldable app guidelines are here, and optimized apps are coming in 2027
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google Play will require apps and games to include dedicated foldable screenshots starting April 2027. 
 All apps should also meet a baseline level of optimization for foldable devices. 
 Developers who ignore the new guidelines won’t be able to publish or update their apps on the Play Store. 

Foldable phones are no longer niche products, and Google seems to have had enough of developers treating them as such. Late last month, the company announced it will start evaluating foldable app quality starting next year. However, it didn’t give too many details. Now, it’s finally filling in the blanks.

Today Google is sharing new quality requirements for foldables, and developers who ignore them won’t be able to publish or update their apps and games on the Play Store. The new requirements are split into two parts. First, there’s a mandatory baseline, called Tier 3, that ensures apps and games work properly when you fold, unfold, or rotate an Android device. This basically means that all apps should perform at least to an acceptable standard on foldable devices.
items.t: Google’s mandatory foldable app guidelines are here, and optimized apps are coming in 2027

items.title: Google Pixel bug is making lock screen transition animations disappear
items.summary:
Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Pixel owners are reporting an issue with the lock screen animation.

 Users are blaming the November update for the missing animation. 

Pixel phones have been dealing with some animation problems as of late. Yesterday, we reported on an animation bug causing visual ghosting when closing an app via the recent apps screen. Now, users are running into a problem with the lock screen animation.

When you lock your Pixel phone, you’ll normally see a subtle animation before the screen turns off. This animation is a fading effect, which sees the screen gradually transition to black. When waking the phone, the same fading effect is used. It serves as a more visually pleasant way to turn your screen off and on than having the screen immediately go dark or turn on.

Samsung's rollout of stable One UI 9 for eligible Galaxy devices is still ongoing, but it has already opened the One UI 9.5 beta program for the Galaxy S26 series, which received the stable One UI 9 update two months ago.

However, the One UI 9.5 beta program isn't open in all regions. It's currently available in Germany, India, Poland, South Korea, the UK, and the US.

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

If you live in any of these countries and don't want to wait for the stable One UI 9.5 update, you can enroll in the One UI 9.5 beta program through the Samsung Members app on your Galaxy S26...
items.t: Samsung announces One UI 9.5 beta program for the Galaxy S26 series in these countries

items.title: Gemini will now let you share your custom Skills and add files from various Google apps
items.summary: Google is upgrading the Gemini app with new skill-sharing capabilities and direct file support, letting users connect real-time documents from Google Drive, Notebook, and Photos straight to their custom AI instructions.

items.title: Spotify is giving every artist a bouncer to keep AI slop off their page
items.summary: Spotify has opened Artist Profile Protection to every artist, letting them review or reject releases delivered under their name. In the default mode, a release you ignore still goes live.
items.t: Spotify is giving every artist a bouncer to keep AI slop off their page

items.title: Motorola starts teasing the Edge 70 Neo, hints at when it will be announced
items.summary:
Motorola has put up a teaser page on Flipkart for the Motorola Edge 70 Neo in India. The company will officially launch the phone on November 24 - next Tuesday.

The images on the page show the phone in a sage-like hue, with a raised rounded-square camera island on the back and a curved display with a centered punch-hole up front. The camera ring reads "50MP", "Ultra HDR", "OIS", and "Lytia". Motorola is also highlighting AI photo editing done just by asking, with "add butterfly on shoulder" as the example prompt.

Motorola Edge 70 Neo teaser images

items.t: Motorola starts teasing the Edge 70 Neo, hints at when it will be announced

items.title: Samsung Galaxy A24 gets One UI 9 based on Android 17
items.summary:
Samsung has started rolling out the Android 17-based One UI 9 update for the Galaxy A24. As usual, the phone's South Korean variant is first in line - it carries model number SM-A245N, and the new software arrives as firmware version A245NKSUBGZJA, bundled with the October 2026 security patch.

The Galaxy A24 launched in 2023 with Android 13 and was promised up to four major OS updates, so One UI 9 is the last big upgrade it will get. The phone received One UI 8.5 back in June, and Samsung started testing One UI 9 for it soon after.

One UI 9 brings more Quick Panel customization...
items.t: Samsung Galaxy A24 gets One UI 9 based on Android 17

items.title: iQOO Z12 Lite shows up in the Google Play Console, has key specs revealed
items.summary:
iQOO's next budget phone has just shown up in the Google Play Console database, which usually means a launch isn't too far off. The iQOO Z12 Lite listing (model number I2510) reveals a front design with a waterdrop notch, along with a few key specs.

According to the listing, the phone is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 6300 chipset (MT6835), comes with 4GB or 6GB of RAM, has a screen with 720x1600 resolution, and runs Android 16.

If that sounds familiar, it's because those are the same specs as the iQOO Z11 Lite, which is actually listed as a variant (with the model number I2515)...
items.t: iQOO Z12 Lite shows up in the Google Play Console, has key specs revealed

items.title: The Sideload 052: Pebble’s back. Now what?
items.summary:
